issue.title: [soundness] N5 zero-map allocation stops at declaration sites: `make([]T, n)` / `[N]T` elements and map-element / closed-channel reads are Go nil maps — accepted programs panic on first write
issue.body:
### The smallest .hy program that demonstrates it

Commit: `main` @ `9f61f54` (latest at time of filing). `hyb` built from that commit (`cargo build -p hyb`, rust 1.99.0); usage banner reports `build pins: go1.26.9 / rust 1.99.0`. Go 1.26.9, darwin/arm64 (also reproduces anywhere: the emitted Go is plain).

Two shapes, one root cause. **(A) allocation sites:**

```hy
// n5_make.hy
struct graph {
    nodes map[int]int
}
fn main() {
    gs := make([]graph, 2)
    gs[0].nodes[1] = 10          // panic: assignment to entry in nil map
    fmt.println("n={len(gs[0].nodes)}")
}
```

**(B) read sites** — the nested-map "group by" idiom:

```hy
// n5_read.hy
fn main() {
    mm := map[string]map[string]int{}
    mm["a"]["b"] = 1             // panic: assignment to entry in nil map
    fmt.println("n={len(mm)}")
}
```

```text
$ hyb check n5_make.hy
n5_make.hy: OK (0 diagnostics)
$ hyb build n5_make.hy -o n5_make && ./n5_make
emitted n5_make.go
built n5_make (go go1.26.9)
panic: assignment to entry in nil map

goroutine 1 [running]:
main.main()
	.../n5_make.go:13 +0x40
exit status 2
```

`n5_read.hy`: identical (`OK (0 diagnostics)` → builds → same panic).

The full 13-shape family (A1–A8 allocation sites, B1–B5 read sites) is tabulated under "Anything else"; every member passes `hyb check` with 0 diagnostics, builds, and dies at its first map write.

### What the checker should say

Nothing — and the programs should run. SPEC-LANGUAGE **N5**: *"`var m map[k]v; m[k] = v` works (first write allocates), where Go panics on a nil map. Why: removes an entire nil-shaped panic class from Hybrid-declared code."* **N3**'s zero-value table: slice / map / set → *"empty (`len` 0; first write allocates — N5)"*, struct → *"field-wise zero values"*. **T8** repeats it. `make([]T, n)` and `[N]T` produce exactly those zero values, n at a time; a missing map element and a closed-channel receive produce the element type's zero value. Per GUARANTEES.md's own severity table this is "a guarantee weaker than documented": the zero-value rows claim a panic class is gone and it is only gone at declaration sites.

If the emitter cannot honor N5 at a site, the fail-closed alternative is a clean diagnostic / `EmitError` — never an accepted program that panics (#645's framing, which the maintainer accepted).

### What it actually said

`OK (0 diagnostics)` for all 13 programs; `hyb build` succeeds; every binary panics `assignment to entry in nil map` at the first write. The emitted Go is a straight transliteration at these sites, e.g. A1 → `gs := make([]graph, 2)`, B1 → `mm["a"]["b"] = 1`.

### Claimed severity

P2 — claim-precision bug (accepted value should have been unproven)

### Anything else

**The family** — every member passes `hyb check` with 0 diagnostics, builds, and dies at its first map write (each is a ≤12-line program; the full set is attached as `repro.zip`, or pasted on request):

| # | shape | zero value produced by |
|---|-------|------------------------|
| A1 | `gs := make([]graph, 2); gs[0].nodes[1] = 10` | `make` element |
| A2 | `ms := make([]map[string]int, 2); ms[0]["a"] = 1` | `make` element (map elem type) |
| A3 | `bs := make([]bag, 0, 4); bs = bs[:1]; bs[0].counts["k"] = 1` | spare capacity exposed by reslice |
| A4 | `s := shelf{bags: make([]bag, 3)}; s.bags[2].counts["k"] = 1` | `make` inside a struct literal |
| A5 | `bs := make([]bag, 2); fill(bs)` where `fill` writes `bs[i].counts[..]` | `make` element reaching a callee |
| A6 | `grid := make([][]map[string]int, 1); grid[0] = make([]map[string]int, 1); grid[0][0]["k"] = 1` | nested `make` |
| A7 | `var arr [2]graph; arr[0].nodes[1] = 10` | array `var` |
| A8 | `bs := [2]bag{}; bs[1].counts["k"] = 1` | array literal with elided elements |
| B1 | `mm := map[string]map[string]int{}; mm["a"]["b"] = 1` | map element read (missing key) |
| B2 | `inner := mm["x"]; inner["k"] = 1` | map element read bound to a local |
| B3 | `g := gs["x"]; g.nodes[1] = 10` with `gs map[string]graph` | map element read of a map-carrying struct |
| B4 | `b, ok := bags["x"]; if !ok { b.counts["k"] = 1 }` | comma-ok read |
| B5 | `ch := make(chan map[string]int, 1); close(ch); m := <-ch; m["k"] = 1` | receive from a closed channel |

Negative controls (same tree, print the expected count): `var m map[string]int`, `var g graph`, `graph{}`, `graph{name: "g"}`, `new(graph)`, nested struct fields, `var s set[int]`, a `var m map` passed to a writing callee, `[]bag{bag{}, bag{}}`, `append(bs, z)` with `var z bag`, `for k, b in bags { b.counts[..] = 1 }` — exactly the sites #662 lowered.

**Root cause.** `zeroinit.rs` (#662, fixes #645) allocates a zero map where it is *declared*: `var` locals, struct literals that leave a map field unkeyed, `new(T)`. Any zero value *produced by an expression* is never seen by that table and stays Go's nil. #662's own text records "arrays of map-carrying structs" and "`make([]bag, n)` elements" as not covered (and #663's close invites a re-worked take for them); generic structs are #744 and named results are #750. The read-site members (B1–B5) are recorded nowhere I could find (issues, PRs, GUARANTEES.md known limits).

**Fix, part 1 — allocation sites (PR to follow, patch ready).** `make` and `[N]T` are declaration sites in disguise: the element type is known structurally, so the existing `n5_zero_init` table applies.
- `make([]T, n[, c])` with an N5-needing `T` → `hy_n5_make(func() T { return <init> }, n[, c])`; a small generic prelude helper (same mechanism as `hy_pop`) that allocates every slot up to the capacity — so A3's reslice-within-cap works — and returns `s[:n]`. Element types whose Go zero value already is Hybrid's (`int`, `plain` structs, channels, maps) keep emitting `make(...)` byte-identical.
- `[N]T` → `n5_zero_init` gains an `Array` arm: `func() (hyArr [N]T) { for i := range hyArr { hyArr[i] = <init> }; return hyArr }()`, one expression for any `N` (literal or const), reachable from `var a [N]T`, `[N]T{}`, struct fields, and `make([][N]T, n)`. A partial literal `[3]bag{{...}}` pads its trailing elements.
- Corpus: `n5-zero-map-allocation-sites.hy` (ACCEPT, byte-exact `EXPECTED-OUTPUT`), 3 hy-emit shape tests, 1 hyb end-to-end test; census surfaces bumped (127 programs: ACCEPT 39 · ACCEPT-MANAGED 2 · REJECT 86).

**Fix, part 2 — read sites (design for the maintainer's call; D11-adjacent).** B1–B5 have no allocation site, only a place, so they need write-site lowering. #663's write-site take was rejected for three concrete reasons; a helper-based lowering answers each:
1. *generic-struct field type text* — a Go generic helper `func hy_n5[K comparable, V any](m *map[K]V) map[K]V { if *m == nil { *m = map[K]V{} }; return *m }` needs no type text at all: Go infers `K`/`V` from the place.
2. *aliased map fields missed* — same: inference sees through `type tally = map[string]int`.
3. *double evaluation* — `hy_n5(&g.nodes)[1] = 10` takes the place's address once; `mm["a"]["b"] = 1` becomes `hy_n5_slot(mm, "a")["b"] = 1` with a get-or-insert helper (`v, ok := m[k]; if !ok || v == nil { v = map[..]{}; m[k] = v }`), evaluating `mm` and `"a"` once each. Both are only emitted at *index-write* sites whose base type is map-carrying (the checker already resolves these shapes for O8/A3), so plain maps stay untouched.
If instead D11 is resolved toward Go-exact for read-produced zero values, N3/N5 should say so and the checker should fail closed (reject or lint) on a write through such a place.

**Rule cited:** SPEC-LANGUAGE §3.1 N3/N5, T8; GUARANTEES.md severity table ("guarantee weaker than documented"). Platform: darwin/arm64, Go 1.26.9, Rust 1.99.0, commit 9f61f54.

**Part 1 Fix PR:** #1208
